summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Toru Kumoi held posts at the Institute for Humanities Informatics and the Japan Institute of Digital Humanities, where he was attested as senior researcher in 2015.

Toru Sagara (1921–2000) was a philosopher and Japanologist. He studied under Tetsuro Watsuji at the University of Tokyo (~1941–1944) and held posts at Ibaraki University (~1953–1966), the University of Tokyo (~1966–1982), and Kyoritsu Women's University (~1982–1993).

Toru Takahashi (1878–1967) worked in Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo, his academic career included professorships at Keijo Imperial University (1926–1940), Fukuoka University (1949), and Tenri University (1950–1964).

Toru Tomabechi (born 1965) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Lausanne, and later served as senior researcher at the Japan Institute of Digital Humanities (~2011) and Institute for Humanities Informatics (~2012).
Toshiaki Yamada (born 1947) is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Toyo University from around 1966 to 1975 and held a post there from around 1978 to 2018.

Toshifumi Goto (born 1947) works in Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (-1982) under Karl Hoffmann and others. He held a professorship at Osaka University and taught at Tohoku University (attested 2003–2012).

Toshihiko Izutsu (1914–1993) worked in philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies. A Keio University graduate, he held long-term posts at Keio (1937–1981), McGill University (1961; 1969–1975), and the Iranian Institute of Philosophy (1975–1979).

Toshihiko Kimura (born 1940) specializes in Indology and philosophy. After studying at Tohoku University (~1959–1963), he held posts at Tokai Gakuin University (~1978–1988), Tohoku University as a part-time lecturer, and International Buddhist University (~2011).

Toshihiro Wada (born 1954) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha in 1981 and held academic appointments at Nagoya University as an associate professor (~1990–2002) and professor (~2002–2020).

Toshiichi Endo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Kelaniya and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (-1995), and held a professorship at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

Toshikazu Watanabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2011), the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2015–2019), and Kokugakuin University (2018).

Toshiki Osada (born 1954) works in linguistics and Indology. After studying at Hokkaido University (~1973–1977), he served as a professor and project leader at the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (~2003–2019) and joined Kyoto University of the Arts (~2019).

Toshinori Ochiai (born 1948) specializes in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Kacho Junior College (~1989–2002), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2002–2019), and directed the Institute for the Study of Ancient Manuscript Buddhist Canons (~2015).
Toshio Ando (1909–1973) was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1928–1931) and held academic posts at Doho University (~1946–1948) and Otani University (~1948–1973).

Toshio Horiuchi (born 1977) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Tokyo (~2002–2009) and held research posts at Toyo University (~2011–2017) and Zhejiang University (~2018).

Toshio Nagahiro (1905–1990) specialized in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kyoto University, he served there and at its Institute for Research in Humanities (1929–1969), later becoming president of Kyoto Tachibana University (1978–1986).
Toshio Sako is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikidō Takasaki and Ekyo Ejima, and at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman.

Toshio Yamazaki (1916–1994) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. His career included posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1950–1955), the University of Tokyo (~1955–1977), Chuo University (~1977–1987), and Hannan University (~1987–1992).

Toshiya Unebe is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Musashi Tachikawa. He served as an associate professor of Indian Studies at Nagoya University (attested 2009).

Totsudo Kato (1870–1949) studied Buddhist and religious studies under Seiran Ouchi, Enryo Inoue, and Banne Shimada, attending Oriental Hall, Kyoto Legal School, and Chuo University. He held teaching posts at Komazawa, Toyo, and Nihon universities.
